title: Mechanical Thoracic Spine Pain
lead: The thoracic spine is a common site of mechanical pain, and a common hiding place for serious disease.
case: A 52-year-old man reports pain between his shoulder blades for 2 days, 7/10, which came on while carrying shopping upstairs and eased after resting. He smokes and has high blood pressure. Palpation of T5 is mildly tender.
> Decision: this is not yet a mechanical diagnosis. Exertional onset, rest relief and cardiac risk factors require urgent medical assessment before physiotherapy.
plan: Screen; educate about mechanical nature and good prognosis.

differentials.name: Mechanical thoracic pain
differentials.key: Movement-related, local stiffness, no systemic signs

differentials.name: Angina or myocardial infarction
differentials.key: Exertional or rest chest/back pain, sweating, breathlessness, risk factors

differentials.name: Pulmonary embolism
differentials.key: Sudden breathlessness, pleuritic pain, fast heart rate, recent surgery or immobility

differentials.name: Aortic dissection
differentials.key: Sudden severe tearing pain, blood pressure difference between arms

differentials.name: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture
differentials.key: Older, osteoporosis, sudden pain after minor load, height loss

differentials.name: Malignancy
differentials.key: Night pain, weight loss, cancer history

differentials.name: Shingles
differentials.key: Burning band pain, rash after a few days

differentials.name: Gallbladder or peptic ulcer
differentials.key: Related to meals, right scapular pain

qa: Why not treat T5? The history suggests possible angina; local tenderness does not exclude it.
Which vital signs would you take? Heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, SpO2, temperature.
What test distinguishes aortic dissection suspicion? Blood pressure in both arms plus history of sudden tearing pain.
A 70-year-old woman on long-term steroids has sudden thoracic pain after a sneeze. What do you suspect? Osteoporotic vertebral fracture; avoid manipulation; refer for imaging.
Why is thoracic pain more worrying than lumbar pain statistically? A higher proportion has visceral or serious causes.

fields.Procedure: Patient sits with arms crossed; actively rotates each way; therapist may add overpressure
fields.Finding and meaning: Comparable pain with restriction supports a mechanical source

fields.Procedure: Prone; therapist's pisiform or thumbs over spinous process; gentle oscillation
fields.Finding and meaning: Comparable pain and stiffness locates a segment

fields.Procedure: Prone or side lying; gentle anterior pressure over rib angle
Sitting slump with neck flexion and knee extension
Tape measure at the 4th intercostal space, full inhalation minus full exhalation
fields.Finding and meaning: Reduced expansion may suggest axial spondyloarthritis or lung disease; compare with norms

redFlags.Finding: Chest or interscapular pain with sweating, nausea, breathlessness
redFlags.Immediate action: Stop; emergency services; keep patient at rest

redFlags.Finding: Sudden tearing pain, BP difference between arms, collapse
Sudden breathlessness, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, calf swelling
Cancer history, weight loss, constant night pain, age over 50
Band-like pain with leg weakness, gait change, brisk reflexes

manual.name: Thoracic thrust manipulation
manual.finding: Comparable stiff, painful segment; no contraindication
manual.application: Supine (patient arms crossed, therapist's hand under the segment, thrust through the arms) or prone
manual.stop: Osteoporosis, fracture risk, fear, any flag

manual.name: Rib mobilisation
manual.application: Prone, gentle oscillation at rib angle

exercise.Exercise: Thoracic extension over chair back or foam roller
exercise.Steps: Hands behind head, extend over the support, return
Side lying, knees bent, open top arm to the other side
Lie face down, raise arms in Y, T and W shapes

modalityNotes: Heat for comfort; TENS optional. Other modalities are not routinely recommended.
pathway: Screen; educate about mechanical nature and good prognosis.
Manual therapy and mobility exercise early.
Strengthening and posture variety; ergonomic adjustments.
